packageRules.description: One weekly PR for all non-major updates, so CI runs once
Keep GitHub Actions bumps in their own weekly PR
Keep pnpm package-manager and workflow pins in the same reviewed update

prBodyTemplate:
## What issue does this solve?

The project still uses the older package versions listed below. This PR proposes newer versions for review. An update alone does not prove that a bug has been fixed.

## Example of the problem

A developer follows the repository setup instructions and gets the current versions in the table. After this change, the same setup uses the proposed versions. We need to check that installation, tests and examples still work.

## Proposal and solution

Update the package versions and the lockfile, which records the exact versions to install. If the same tool is used in several workflows, keep those versions aligned. Run the required checks before merging.

## Why this is better

Reviewers can see the exact changes together and check whether the project still works with them. Claims about speed or security need their own evidence.

## Before and after

The table shows each current version and its proposed replacement:

{{{table}}}

## Evidence and results

The version files show what changed. Review the current CI results and raw logs, then record the observed test results before merging. This description generator does not establish that the updated packages work in this project.

{{{warnings}}}
{{{notes}}}

## How to use it in everyday work

After merge, follow the repository setup instructions and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Run the usual checks. Keep related setup instructions and workflows in sync. A package update does not itself authorize a release or deployment.
